text:
St. Louis is stuck in the middle of the Central and trending the wrong way. The Blues are winless in three (0-2-1) after Saturday's 3-1 loss in Nashville, and the chances say the slide is real: 38% of the expected goals in that stretch. They are 7-8-2 with 48% of the expected goals, and their 16 points are close to what the play has earned. Our simulations put them at 85 points and a 27% playoff chance.

There have been moments. Thursday in New Jersey they came back from 4-1 down in the third to force overtime before losing, with Philip Broberg and Dalibor Dvorsky scoring 4-4 in a hurry. Broberg's pairing with Adam Jiricek has been their best, 55% of the expected goals and a 6-4 goal edge. The reunited top line of Robert Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud has been fine without being dangerous: 52% of the chances, 6-6 in goals.

The worries are the depth lines and the blue line's top pair. Cam Fowler and Brandon Carlo have been outscored 9-4 at an even split of chances, which looks more like bad luck than bad play. Justin Barron has eight points in ten on 3.7 expected, a heater that will cool. What to watch: whether Joel Hofer, the most written-about Blue, can steal a few while the five-on-five game sorts itself out.
